cues.en: Hello everybody, my name is Martin Kleppmann and I'm going to be giving the next eight lectures on distributed systems. This is the second half of the course on concurrent and distributed systems. And so in the first half of this course, you've seen a lot on concurrency that occurs within a single process. So when you have...
cues.zh: 大家好，我叫 Martin Kleppmann，接下来会为大家讲授分布式系统的八节课。这是并发与分布式系统课程的后半部分。课程前半部分，我们讲了很多单个进程内的并发问题。比如，当你有……

cues.en: especially when you have multiple threads within a single process that are performing operation concurrently, you have seen how to deal with mutual exclusion, for example, and various algorithms for ensuring safe concurrency. Now, in this kind of concurrent system, you have all of the threads
cues.zh: 尤其是当单个进程中有多个线程在并发执行操作时，我们讲过如何处理互斥，以及如何用各种算法确保并发安全。在这种并发系统中，所有线程通常

cues.en: usually sharing a single address space and so you can just pass a variable from one thread to another thread and that variable can contain pointers or references to arbitrary objects and this will work because the memory addresses that one thread can access are the same as the memory addresses that another thread can access. Now when we move to distributed systems this changes. So in distributed systems we still have concurrency, we still have multiple processes and multiple threads
cues.zh: 共享同一个地址空间，所以你可以把一个变量从一个线程传给另一个线程。这个变量可以包含指向任意对象的指针或引用，而且这样做行得通，因为一个线程能够访问的内存地址，另一个线程也能访问。现在转向分布式系统后，情况就变了。在分布式系统中，我们仍然有并发，仍然可能有多个进程和多个线程

cues.en: performing operations concurrently potentially, but we also have the additional challenge that now we're talking about not just a single program running on a single computer, but multiple programs running on multiple computers where those computers are communicating via a network. And this aspect that we are now introducing this network is part of what makes a distributed system distributed. Another aspect is also that we don't have a single shared address space anymore.
cues.zh: 同时执行操作，但还面临一个额外的挑战：我们讨论的不再是单台计算机上运行的单个程序，而是多台计算机上运行的多个程序，它们通过网络通信。引入网络这一点，是分布式系统之所以分布式的原因之一。另一个方面是，我们不再拥有单一的共享地址空间。

cues.en: So a pointer that makes sense in one process, if you send it over the network to another process running on a different computer, that pointer will not necessarily make any sense to the recipient of that message. And so we have to think about different ways of sharing data between these concurrent entities. So a definition of a distributed system, a somewhat joking definition provided by Leslie Lamport,
cues.zh: 所以，在一个进程中有意义的指针，如果通过网络发给另一台计算机上的进程，接收方不一定能理解这个指针。因此，我们必须考虑在这些并发实体之间共享数据的其他方式。Leslie Lamport 给分布式系统下过一个带点玩笑意味的定义：

cues.en: is that a distributed system is a system in which the failure of a computer you didn't even know existed can render your own computer unusable. Whether this is a good definition or not we can debate but Leslie Lamport is a bit of a legend in the area of distributed systems and we will see various aspects of work that he's done over the decades and of course lots of other people have done work in this area and we will see that over the course of these lectures.
cues.zh: 分布式系统就是这样一种系统：一台你甚至不知道存在的计算机发生故障，就能让你自己的计算机无法使用。这个定义好不好，可以讨论。不过，Leslie Lamport 是分布式系统领域的传奇人物之一。接下来我们会看到他几十年来的一些研究成果，当然也会了解许多其他人在这一领域的工作。

cues.en: More generally I think I would define a distributed system as one in which you have got multiple computers or computing devices. These devices might be smartphones, they might be robots, they might be self-driving cars, they might be desktop computers, they might be servers in a data center, so any sort of computing device really. And these computing devices are communicating via some kind of network, which might be the internet, and they are trying to achieve some kind of task together.
cues.zh: 更一般地说，我认为分布式系统是由多台计算机或计算设备组成的系统。这些设备可能是智能手机、机器人、自动驾驶汽车、台式机，也可能是数据中心里的服务器，基本上任何计算设备都算。这些设备通过某种网络通信，比如互联网，并共同完成某项任务。

cues.en: the study of distributed systems is really the study of how do we coordinate the activities of these different devices in such a way that they achieve together the task that they are trying to achieve. So I will start with a little bit of background first just the administrative things to get that done. So first of all if you want any further background reading on this course hopefully the lecture notes will be reasonably self-contained but of course further
cues.zh: 分布式系统的研究，本质上就是研究如何协调这些不同设备的活动，使它们能够共同完成想要完成的任务。我先从一点点背景讲起，首先是行政事务方面的事。首先，如果你想进一步了解这门课程的背景资料，希望讲义本身已经相当完整，当然如果感兴趣的话，书中还有更多

cues.en: detail is available in books if you're interested. There are several different styles of books that I've put here on the list. So the textbook by Van Steen and Tannenbaum is a sort of systems level overview. So this is, it comes at distributed systems from quite an applied angle of real applications that real people use and discusses how these work.
cues.zh: 细节可供参考。我在这个书单上列了几种不同风格的书。Van Steen 和 Tannenbaum 的教科书是一种系统层面的综述，它从相当应用的角度出发，讲的是真实用户使用的真实应用，并讨论这些应用是如何工作的，

cues.en: and discusses the various implementation details of it. It doesn't go as far into the theory as some of the other books, but it's more practically oriented. If you like the theory, then the second book on this list is a good choice. So the textbook by Kachin, Gaurari and Rodriguez is an excellent but quite detailed overview of distributed systems theory. So it goes into a lot more depth than we have time to talk about in this course. But if you want to read more about the theory, this is an excellent book.
cues.zh: 还会讨论各种实现细节。它不像其他一些书那样深入理论，但更偏实践。如果你喜欢理论，那么书单上的第二本书是个不错的选择。Cachin、Guerraoui 和 Rodrigues 的教科书是一份出色但相当详尽的分布式系统理论综述，它的深度远超我们这门课有时间讲到的内容。如果你想进一步阅读理论方面的内容，这是一本极好的书。

cues.en: I also wrote a book in this area called Designing Data Intensive Applications. This book is a bit more oriented towards distributed database systems, so it's not just distributed systems in general, there's a lot of the other databases content in there, and this book is more oriented towards industrial software engineers, so people who are working professionally with distributed databases will probably find this kind of book useful.
cues.zh: 我自己也写了一本这个领域的书，叫《Designing Data Intensive Applications》。这本书更偏向分布式数据库系统，所以它不只是讲一般的分布式系统，里面有大量数据库相关的内容，而且这本书更面向工业界的软件工程师，也就是那些专业从事分布式数据库工作的人，很可能会觉得这本书有用。

cues.en: And finally, there's the Bacon and Harris textbook, which was already recommended for the concurrent systems part of this course, which really provides the link between operating systems and distributed systems. Okay, so this course is also connected to various other courses in the tripos. Most obviously concurrent systems that this course is part of. Also operating systems, which you studied last year. So all of the background that you had there on...
cues.zh: 最后还有 Bacon 和 Harris 的教科书，这门课程的并发系统部分已经推荐过它，它真正地把操作系统和分布式系统联系了起来。好，这门课还与 tripos 里的其他几门课程相关联。最明显的就是它所属的并发系统课。还有操作系统，你们去年学过的。所以你在那里学到的所有背景知识，比如

cues.en: processes and inter-process communication and scheduling of processes, all of that stuff is relevant for this course. Also the databases course is connected to distributed systems because as I mentioned just now many modern databases are in fact distributed and they use a lot of the techniques that we will talk about in this course and so using modern databases often involves using distributed systems as well. There's a strong connection between distributed systems and computer networking because as I said
cues.zh: 进程、进程间通信以及进程调度，这些内容都与这门课相关。另外，数据库课程也与分布式系统有关联，因为正如我刚才提到的，许多现代数据库实际上是分布式的，它们用到了我们这门课将讲到的很多技术，所以使用现代数据库往往也意味着使用分布式系统。分布式系统和计算机网络之间也有很强的联系，因为正如我所说，

cues.en: distributed systems involve network communication generally. The difference between the two courses is that the computer networking course is mostly about how do you actually get the bytes over the wire from one device to the other device. So what did the network protocols look like that enable devices to communicate and then
cues.zh: 分布式系统通常涉及网络通信。这两门课的区别在于，计算机网络课主要讲的是如何真正地把字节通过线路从一台设备传到另一台设备，也就是让设备能够相互通信的那些网络协议是什么样的，然后

cues.en: distributed systems builds on top of computer networking and saying, OK, assuming we now have this mechanism for devices to communicate, how can we now ensure that these devices behave in the ways that we want? There's connection to further Java. So there's programming exercises that involve a bit of distributed computing. The security aspect of distributed systems are very interesting and they are covered in a course in Easter term.
cues.zh: 分布式系统是在计算机网络的基础上再往上构建，也就是：好，假设我们现在已经有了这种设备间的通信机制，那我们如何确保这些设备按照我们想要的方式运作？此外还有进阶 Java 课程的联系，那里的编程练习会涉及一些分布式计算。分布式系统的安全方面也非常有意思，它们会在复活节学期的一门课中讲到。

cues.en: that's dedicated just to the topic of security and finally next year's cloud computing course builds upon distributed systems because cloud computing is all about being able to flexibly process large amounts of data and if you have sufficiently large amounts of data you generally need a distributed system in order to process it. Okay so I gave a brief definition of
cues.zh: 这是一门专门讲安全的课程。最后，明年的云计算课程会建立在分布式系统的基础之上，因为云计算的核心就是灵活地处理海量数据，而如果数据量足够大，你通常就需要一个分布式系统来处理它。好，我简单介绍了

cues.en: what a distributed system is. The next question is then why? Like, why should we go to all of this effort of making a system distributed? Why can't we just use a single computer and keep things simple? And well, one reason is that some applications, some types of things you want to do, computers are inherently distributed. So if you want to send a message from your phone to your friend's phone, this inevitably involves two different phones and a network.
cues.zh: 什么是分布式系统。下一个问题是：为什么要这样做？为什么我们要费这么大力气把系统做成分布式的？为什么不能用一台计算机，把事情保持简单呢？嗯，一个原因是，对于某些应用、某些你想做的事情，计算机天然就是分布式的。比如你想从你的手机发消息到你朋友的手机，这必然涉及两台不同的设备和一张网络。

cues.en: So this is a distributed system, there's no way around it, there's no way of building a messaging system that is not distributed if you want to be able to communicate across different devices. And so building this type of software is one reason why we might be interested in distributed systems, but there are many other reasons as well. So another good reason for being interested in distributed systems is that it actually allows us to make systems more reliable. And the reason for this is, say you have multiple computers
cues.zh: 所以这就是一个分布式系统，绕不开——如果你想跨设备通信，就不可能构建一个非分布式的消息系统。构建这类软件是我们对分布式系统感兴趣的原因之一，但还有很多别的原因。对分布式系统感兴趣的另一个好理由是，它实际上能让系统更可靠。原因在于，假设你有多台计算机，

cues.en: which are each performing part of some job. If one of those fails, maybe one of them has to be rebooted, for example, or one of them has a hardware failure, then maybe the remaining computers can take over the work from the failed computer. And so now this allows the system as a whole to continue functioning, even though one of the computers involved in it has actually gone down. Another reason we might want to make systems distributed is
cues.zh: 每台都在执行某个任务的一部分。如果其中一台出了故障，比如其中一台需要重启，或者一台发生了硬件故障，那么剩下的计算机也许可以接管故障计算机的工作。这样一来，即使其中一台计算机真的宕机了，整个系统仍然可以继续运转。我们可能想把系统做成分布式的另一个原因是

cues.en: for better performance. So for example, in internet distributed systems, you might have users all around the world. You might have some users in the UK, some users in the US, some users in New Zealand, some users in South Africa, wherever. And there are large distances between these different places. And so network communication from one of these places to the others is always going to take a little while. You're talking at least 100 milliseconds.
cues.zh: 为了获得更好的性能。举例来说，在互联网分布式系统中，用户可能遍布世界各地。可能有用户在英国，有用户在美国，有用户在新西兰，有用户在南非，随便哪儿都有。而这些地方之间相距遥远。所以从一个地方到另一个地方的网络通信总是要花一点时间。至少也要 100 毫秒起步，

cues.en: simply because of the speed of light that it takes for communication to travel from one continent to another. And so one reason why people are interested in distributed systems is to make systems faster by putting data closer to where the people are. So if you have some users in multiple different continents you can have computers in multiple different continents and if you have each user communicating with the computer that is most local to them
cues.zh: 这仅仅是因为光速的限制，通信从一个大陆传到另一个大陆就需要这么久。所以人们对分布式系统感兴趣的一个原因，就是把数据放到离用户更近的地方，从而让系统更快。比如你的用户分布在多个不同的大洲，你就可以在多个大洲都部署计算机，让每个用户都和离他们最近的计算机通信，

cues.en: then you avoid the long distance intercontinental communication as part of the delays that are added to their communication. So making systems distributed allows us to make them faster, potentially. And finally, another reason why people build distributed systems is to solve bigger problems than they could with a single computer. So some computing problems are simply very large scale. So think of scientific computing examples, like, for example, the CERN.
cues.zh: 这样就能避免跨洲长距离通信带来的额外延迟。所以把系统做成分布式的有可能让它们更快。最后，人们构建分布式系统的另一个原因，是解决单台计算机无法应付的更大规模的问题。有些计算问题规模实在太大。想想科学计算的例子，比如欧洲核子研究中心（CERN）。

cues.en: The particle accelerator in Switzerland that includes the Large Hadron Collider, they have a vast computing infrastructure involving a million CPU cores and God knows how many hard disks in order to just take all of the data that they're gathering from the particle accelerator and process it and analyze it and try to use this to discover new particles, for example. Now, this scale of task would simply be not...
cues.zh: 瑞士的粒子加速器，包括 Large Hadron Collider，拥有庞大的计算基础设施，涉及上百万个 CPU 核心和天知道多少块硬盘，只是为了接收他们从粒子加速器收集的所有数据，处理、分析，并尝试用它来发现新粒子等等。现在，这种规模的任务根本无法……

cues.en: be possible to achieve on a single computer because there is no supercomputer that is big enough to be able to handle these vast volumes of data. So simply solving this problem of analyzing such large volumes of data has to be done on a network of lots of small computers and those computers have to distribute the work amongst them and they have to work together in order to achieve the tasks that the scientists are trying to do.
cues.zh: 在单台计算机上实现，因为没有哪台超级计算机大到足以处理如此海量的数据。所以，要解决分析如此大规模数据的问题，只能在由许多小型计算机组成的网络上完成，这些计算机必须彼此分配工作，并协同工作，才能完成科学家们想做的任务。

cues.en: This is really one of the another key area in which we can use distributed systems is to solve bigger problems. Now, those are the advantages of making systems distributed. There are unfortunately some significant disadvantages as well. And the main disadvantage that you will be well familiar with is whenever you're trying to do something over a network, that network might not be working for some reason. And so
cues.zh: 这确实是我们可以用分布式系统来解决更大问题的另一个关键领域。这些就是让系统分布化的优势。不幸的是，也有一些重大劣势。而你会很熟悉的主要劣势是：每当你尝试通过网络做某件事时，网络可能因某种原因无法工作。所以

cues.en: everyone has experienced what it's like for the internet to be down or for your Wi-Fi signal to be weak or for, you know, in some rural part of the country and your cellular data signal is weak and you're trying to load a map or something like that, everyone has experienced this kind of frustration before and, well, the study of distributed systems is all about the study of such frustrations. So we assume whenever we are building a distributed system that involves communication over a network
cues.zh: 每个人都经历过互联网断网，或者 Wi-Fi 信号很弱，或者，你知道，在某些乡村地区，蜂窝数据信号很弱，而你正想加载地图之类的东西，每个人都经历过这种挫败感；而分布式系统的研究，正是研究这类挫败感。所以，每当我们构建涉及通过网络通信的分布式系统时，我们都假设

cues.en: that networks are not perfectly reliable. And so it is always possible for communication to fail. It is always possible that because if it's a Wi-Fi network, you might be out of range. If it's a wired network, somebody might have unplugged the wrong cable.
cues.zh: 网络并非完全可靠。因此，通信始终可能失败。始终可能——如果是 Wi-Fi 网络，你可能超出范围；如果是有线网络，可能有人拔错了网线。

cues.en: any type of network it might just be temporarily overloaded and so it might be dropping messages, maybe even somebody might be maliciously trying to interfere with the network and cause it to drop packets, maybe causing a denial of service attack for example. There are many reasons why communication might not work from time to time and so we have to build systems that are robust so that even if communication is interrupted from time to time the system as a whole still.
cues.zh: 任何类型的网络都可能只是暂时过载，因而可能丢消息；甚至可能有人恶意干扰网络，导致它丢包，比如造成拒绝服务攻击。通信时不时无法工作的原因有很多，所以我们必须构建健壮的系统，这样即使通信偶尔中断，整个系统仍然

cues.en: functions in some correct way where of course we can define what we mean with correct but we want it to continue functioning. Another thing that can go wrong in distributed systems is that some of the processes, the running the code, might crash and for example if you have a system consisting of multiple computers and you reboot one of them you probably want the remaining computers to carry on the task of serving user requests and so
cues.zh: 能以某种正确的方式运行——当然我们可以定义“正确”指什么——但我们希望它继续运行。分布式系统中另一件可能出错的事是，一些运行代码的进程可能崩溃。例如，如果你的系统由多台计算机组成，你重启其中一台，你大概希望其余计算机继续执行服务用户请求的任务，所以

cues.en: What we want here is that one of the processes is temporarily out of action and we want the system as a whole to still continue nevertheless. And finally, all of these failures can happen non-deterministically and that is we simply don't know when they happen, they could happen at any moment, unpredictably, and we still have to ensure that the software works nevertheless. So what we often strive for in distributed systems is what is called as what is known as fault tolerance.
cues.zh: 我们这里想要的是，其中一个进程暂时停止工作，而整个系统仍然要继续运行。最后，所有这些故障都可能以非确定性方式发生，也就是说，我们根本不知道它们何时发生，它们可能在任何时刻不可预测地发生，而我们仍必须确保软件照常工作。所以，我们在分布式系统中经常追求的就是所谓的容错。

cues.en: which means that even if some part of the system is faulty, some part of the system is not working, the system as a whole still continues providing the service to the users. And so this is one of the main challenges in distributed systems. How do we make things in such a way that they can tolerate faults? In fact, making things
cues.zh: 这意味着，即使系统的某部分出了故障、某部分无法正常工作，系统整体仍能继续为用户提供服务。这是分布式系统的主要挑战之一：我们如何设计系统，让它能够容错？事实上，要做到容错……

cues.en: distributed and fault tolerant is so difficult that a lot of people who work professionally on distributed systems think that, oh well, if you can solve a problem on a single computer, it's basically easy. So if you can solve a problem on a single computer, you'll probably have a much better time just keeping it on one computer, not overcomplicating things, not going into a distributed system setting.
cues.zh: ……并且做到分布式和容错是如此困难，以至于很多专业从事分布式系统工作的人认为：嗯，如果你能在单台计算机上解决一个问题，那基本上就是简单的。所以如果你能在单机上解决问题，通常最好就把它留在单机上，不要过度复杂化，不要引入分布式系统的架构。

cues.en: All of the problems, this Pandora's box of problems that arise with distributed systems, well we should try and open that only if we actually have to. But as we said earlier there are lots of good reasons why you might have to open that box.
cues.zh: 面对分布式系统带来的这一系列问题——这个潘多拉魔盒——我们应该只在真正不得已的时候才去打开它。但正如我们之前所说，有很多充分的理由会让你不得不打开这个盒子。
